summary: track rate/note/drop/progress resolve a title only if it is already in the local library: a missing row is a usage error with the add-this-first hint (exit 2), while a store failure stays a plain error (exit 1) and never prints usage.
reason: Unlike track progress, rate/note/drop built a synthetic entry when the id was absent and upserted it, so a typo silently created a title-less library row that polluted listings, exports, and analytics. Two follow-on invariants matter as much as the guard itself: (1) the not-found case must be distinguishable from a store failure, or a locked/corrupt database is reported as bad arguments with a usage dump; the sentinel errMalNotInLibrary carries that distinction; (2) (kind,id) is the table's primary key, so the guard reads that one row instead of scanning and sorting the whole kind.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'TestTrackMutationsRejectAbsentIDs|TestTrackMutationStoreFailureIsNotAUsageError|TestTrackMutationAdvancesUpdatedAt' asserts exit 2 with the add hint and a zero-row library for an unadded id, a non-2 exit with no usage text when the store is broken, and a freshly stamped updated_at after a mutation.
